title: Corporate climate action plan approved
subtitle: Parkland fee refund for a Woodside Road renovation, CAO objectives, Sloan Hill Park closed-session direction, and by-laws.
overview: Council approved the Corporate Climate Action Plan {{vote:m4}}, a roadmap for cutting energy use and greenhouse gas emissions from city operations such as buildings, transit and fleet, water and wastewater facilities, and solar generation. Approval comes with a condition: delivery depends on the pace of capital investment. Staff said many projects will return through future multi-year budgets and annual climate reporting, and that grants and alternative financing will be explored.

Council also granted a petition from the owners of a home at 53 Woodside Road. It exempted the renovation project from parkland dedication cash-in-lieu and directed staff to reimburse the payments already made {{vote:m7}}. Staff advised that council could only grant a full exemption, not a partial one. The petitioners said they would donate part of the refund back to the parkland reserve.

Earlier, council approved the Chief Administrative Officer's 2026 performance objectives {{vote:m2}}. After the first closed session, the mayor reported that council gave direction to staff on Sloan Hill Park encroachments. The CAO is expected to present the objectives in open session in the coming weeks.

decisions.detail: Council approved the plan for reducing energy use and emissions from city operations, with implementation subject to the pace of capital investment.
Council exempted the renovation project from parkland dedication cash-in-lieu and directed staff to reimburse the owners for payments already made.
Council approved the proposed 2026 performance review objectives for the Chief Administrative Officer, as set out in the report dated January 20, 2026.

debate: Delegates on the climate plan asked for more. One wanted the plan to calculate and report the embodied emissions of road and bridge construction, add related requirements to procurement, and phase out free parking passes for city and police staff.

A second delegate welcomed the plan but noted that five major projects fall outside the ten-year capital plan. The delegate proposed researching a community-invested solar project at the Eastview landfill, in which residents could invest small amounts and the city would buy the power.

Councillors asked why Eastview was the focus and about other sites such as parking lots. The delegate cited the landfill's much larger capacity. Staff cautioned about landfill gas monitoring, natural heritage and other uses of the land. One councillor also noted that grid contracts now compete across technologies.

On the Woodside Road petition, the delegate said building department advice that there was no rush led to permits being filed just after the schedule of standard property values rose, adding about $21,000. The delegate also said the owners would have paid the earlier amount.

Staff said the by-law was applied correctly and that the Planning Act does not allow individual rates, so council could only grant a full exemption or none. Some councillors raised concerns about precedent and the lack of public notice. The mover argued the case was unique and called for fairness.
